rules.title: Manifest does not match extension behavior
guidance: Check that titles, descriptions, commands, categories, preferences, capabilities, setup, material non-obvious services, dependencies, and limitations accurately describe the implementation.
Use blocking severity for an obvious factual mismatch, an extension description that describes different behavior, or a command name or description that is clearly misleading about what it runs.
Use suggestion severity for wording polish, minor clarity improvements, or other non-misleading copy edits.
Do not report schema or other mechanically verifiable validity checks owned by CI.

rules.title: Dependency choice does not match implementation
guidance: Flag unused, unexpectedly powerful, incoherent, or needlessly redundant dependencies.
Recommend a compatible current @vicinae/api version when useful and remind the author to run npm install and commit package-lock.json.

rules.title: Asset does not match its stated purpose
guidance: Flag deceptive, executable, meaningfully unauditable, or unexplained generated assets.
Do not report mechanically verifiable paths, dimensions, or aspect ratios owned by CI, or reject ordinary images merely for using a binary format.

rules.title: Unsafe downloaded executable
guidance: Reject arbitrary downloaded binaries.
Allow a justified resource from an established independent source; prefer asking users to install required tools themselves.

rules.title: Command or code injection
guidance: Flag unsafe shell construction, eval, Function, decoded executable strings, concealed dynamic imports, and equivalent unintended execution paths.
Do not flag safely parameterized process arguments merely because they contain user input.

rules.title: Credential or sensitive-data exposure
guidance: Flag credentials embedded in source, logged, sent to unrelated services, or exposed to commands that do not need them.
Use LocalStorage from @vicinae/api for persistent sensitive extension data instead of Cache, ad-hoc files, system keychains, Secret Service, wallets, or platform credential utilities.
Flag direct system credential-store integration when LocalStorage covers the use case; Vicinae should own storage portability and lifecycle.
For OAuth access and refresh tokens, use OAuth.PKCEClient.setTokens, getTokens, and removeTokens from @vicinae/api.

rules.title: Unsafe or unjustified native process execution
guidance: Identify spawned programs and confirm their purpose matches the extension.
Flag unsafe execution and children that can outlive Vicinae; allow legitimate documented system-tool dependencies.

rules.title: Environment-specific behavior duplicates @vicinae/api
guidance: Actively inspect the current @vicinae/api declarations for a functionally equivalent portable replacement.
Allow essential environment-specific behavior when no equivalent Vicinae API exists.
Use blocking severity when @vicinae/api obviously covers the complete use case and replacement is unambiguous. Do not report this rule when equivalence is uncertain.

If the replacement needs a newer @vicinae/api version, recommend the minimum compatible version when known, otherwise the current provided version; remind the author to run npm install and commit package-lock.json.

rules.title: Suspicious or deceptive network usage
guidance: Allow network access without a finding when the endpoint reasonably supports the extension's stated purpose, including ordinary APIs and services implied by that purpose.
Flag unrelated or suspicious destinations, concealed data transmission, undisclosed analytics or tracking, credential or personal-data exfiltration, and clearly unsafe endpoints.
Do not create a finding merely to inventory legitimate endpoints or demand that obvious service usage be justified.

rules.title: Missing actionable error feedback
guidance: Require useful feedback for operational failures, missing tools, and unsupported environments.
Do not require redundant handling when Vicinae already presents the failure clearly.

rules.title: Missing loading or empty-state feedback
guidance: Distinguish observable loading, empty, successful, and failed states.
Do not require loading UI for effectively immediate work or flows handled by a Vicinae component.

rules.title: Material logic error causes wrong behavior
guidance: Flag high-confidence logic errors that cause the extension's core behavior to produce materially wrong results, perform the wrong action, corrupt or lose data, or fail in realistic common usage.
Use warning severity for a significant but non-blocking defect affecting a realistic workflow.
Do not report speculative problems, unlikely edge cases, minor inconsistencies, cosmetic defects, or low-impact logic errors—not even as suggestions.
Trace the concrete execution path and state the observable wrong behavior; do not report this rule without clear evidence from the changed code.

rules.title: Duplicates native Vicinae functionality
guidance: Use the trusted current product documentation and flag obvious replicas with no meaningful distinction, such as a generic emoji picker.
Allow integrations with external tools or services and extensions providing distinct data, workflows, or capabilities.
Report only documented, substantially equivalent built-in functionality with no clear added value.

rules.title: Obfuscated, minified, dead, or generated code
guidance: Reject source that cannot be meaningfully audited; otherwise flag dead paths, commented-out development blocks, and unexplained generated code.

rules.title: Behavior does not match its presentation
guidance: Flag concrete misleading names, hidden behavior, description mismatches, concealed execution, or unexplained data transmission; do not report vague suspicion.
